rows.analysis: Closest wording to a waste-and-overflow replacement, but no access route, drywall restoration, permit, cleanup or warranty line is supplied.

rows.scope_owner: Lever, plug and spout with diverter; labor and materials
rows.analysis: “Spout/diverter” may describe a different assembly. Confirm parts and contracting entity; shared address/phone with Save-On-Interior does not establish common ownership.
Adjustment-only wording is not a replacement-plus-access price. Silence about drywall is not proof of exclusion; ask for the written scope.

official_fees.item: Category 1P — single residential unit fixture/shower pan/kitchen-bath remodel, max two inspections
official_fees.note: Conditional category; not a confirmed job fee or total price.

analysis: The supplied amounts are owner reports, not independently verified prices. They are shown only in an owner-reported column; verified amounts remain blank.
The arithmetic spread is $479 and the highest supplied amount is about 4.55 times the lowest, but the scopes differ, so this is not a market range or a like-for-like comparison.
None of the supplied scopes explicitly mentions opening and restoring the storage-unit ceiling. Silence is not an exclusion; obtain a combined written scope.
Do not add the official permit fee to a quote until the quote says whether permits/inspections are included and DBI confirms the category.

cost_drivers.driver: Scope depth: handle adjustment vs full waste-and-overflow replacement
cost_drivers.detail: Fast Response's $135 owner-reported figure reflects 'Repair/adjust bath tub wastewater plunger handle' (surface diagnostic/linkage call), whereas Expert's $614 owner-reported figure covers 'Replacing waste and overflow' (concealed assembly/labor), and Bay Area's $550 owner-reported quote cites plug lever + spout with diverter.

cost_drivers.driver: Access route: tub-side overflow extraction vs below-ceiling opening
cost_drivers.detail: If a technician extracts/frees the mechanism via the tub overflow plate without damaging concealed piping, demolition and ceiling restoration costs stay near zero. Dropping down to the storage ceiling adds wall/ceiling access, concealed tee/pipe risk, and finish restoration.

cost_drivers.driver: Drywall restoration, paint, and serviceable access panel (B / C-9 trade)
cost_drivers.detail: None of the three C-36-only estimate providers explicitly priced drywall patch, tape, texture, prime/paint, or a framed access panel. Either hire a dual-licensed B + C-36 lead (Ace #1 / Rapid Flow #2) with named finish scope or pair a C-36 specialist (Atlas #3) with Bernal Hill Drywall (#6).

cost_drivers.driver: SF DBI permit & inspection schedule (July 2026 Table 1A-C)
cost_drivers.impact: $290–$320+ permit + inspection fees if pipes are cut/replaced
cost_drivers.detail: DBI requires a permit before cutting into or replacing concealed piping. Official fees (eff. 2026-07-12): Category 1P $290 (max 2 inspections) or 11P/M $320; regular inspection $519/hr; off-hour $555/hr; reinspection $259/half-hr. Separate tenant spaces can affect permit count.

cost_drivers.driver: Contractor size, insurance model, remodel focus & dispatch geography
cost_drivers.detail: Full-service insured firms (~20 staff, active WC, BBB A+ / Diamond Certified like Ace #1 & Atlas #3) carry higher overhead than solo WC-exempt operators. Remodel-heavy GCs (We Do #4, $400-$800/sf site focus) or East Bay dispatchers (Plumbing 1 #11 in Hayward) may add mobilization or bridge travel surcharges.

cost_drivers.driver: Concealed pipe corrosion, tenant notice & pre-1978 environmental screening
cost_drivers.detail: Older SF brass/galvanized/cast-iron drains can fracture under extraction, triggering pipe-section replacement and DBI rough inspection before closure. Civil Code §1954 tenant notice (24h presumed reasonable), water shut-off windows, and conditional EPA RRP lead-safe containment apply if painted finishes are cut.
